title: Corn, fresh, cooked, fat added, NS (fat type)

content.title: About
content.content: Corn is a worldwide cultivated grain. This product consists of fresh ears that are boiled until tender and then sautéed with added fat. The preparation preserves the natural sweetness of the kernels and enhances their aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn was first domesticated over 7,000 years ago in Mexico and is one of the oldest cultivated crops.
There are more than 300 varieties of corn, differing in color, size, and flavor.
Beyond food, corn is used to produce bio‑fuel, plastics, and cosmetics.
The fat content of the final product depends on the type of added fat – vegetable or butter.
Carotenoids give some corn varieties their bright yellow hue.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn provides slowly digestible carbs that help maintain satiety over time.

items.title: Rich in vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 supports protein metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids and phenolic compounds help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in corn promotes healthy bowel movements.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Added vegetable fat enriches the dish with mono‑ and poly‑unsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to corn.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The added fat increases the energy density, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: While corn is naturally gluten‑free, processing may introduce trace gluten.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet corn can raise blood glucose levels, which is relevant for people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn can be enjoyed on its own, added to salads, soups, stews, or used as a side dish. Garnish with fresh herbs or spices before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked corn in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags.
